- We need to qualify streaming first-token latency (p50/p95), sustained concurrency, and burst tolerance.
- We'll share a representative prompt seed and traffic profile (attached) — can your team run a first-pass baseline and share artifacts?

Targets we're trying to validate:
- p50 first-token latency: ~120ms
- p95 first-token latency: <300ms
- Sustained concurrency: 50 concurrent streams
- Burst: 200 concurrent for up to 30s

Appreciate a short confirmation on measurement definitions and any requirements for the harness. Timeline: can you run initial runs and report by Wed 2027-07-26?

Subject: Re: SLO qualification: latency & throughput measurement definitions + prompt seed

Thanks Jordan — great to align.

Quick recap and proposed measurement definitions (so we have a shared spec):

1) Latency definitions
- First-token latency (streaming): time from request received by edge to first token emitted (p50/p95 over test run).
- End-to-end completion latency (non-streaming): request->final-token emitted.
- Measurement note: clocks will use server-side timestamps; we'll also record client-side timings when available.

2) Throughput & concurrency
- Throughput: measured as requests/sec (RPS) and tokens/sec produced, sampled across the steady-state window.
- Concurrency: number of actively open response streams (sustained vs peak burst periods).

3) Streaming specifics
- Warm KV-cache pass: include an initial warmup phase (10 minutes or N requests) before steady-state measurement.
- Backpressure simulation: harness will exercise simultaneous slow-consuming clients to surface tail latency.

4) Reproducibility
- We'll version the prompt seed and traffic profile; please include token length distributions and labels for prompt categories.
- Determinism: we'll pin model weights and runtime quantization/par and record runtime config (batching, kernels, mem alloc).

Action items for your team
- Share the prompt seed + traffic profile (we got the attachments) and call out any prompts that must be excluded for PII.
- Confirm the acceptance windows (you suggested p95 <300ms) and whether we should target a more conservative p50.

I'll attach a measurement_spec_v1.md that captures the above and the harness command lines we'll use. We'll aim to get a baseline run and a short summary back by 2027-07-26.

Best,
Dev Patel
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: measurement_spec_v1.md (text/markdown)

> Quick recap and proposed measurement definitions (so we have a shared spec):

Adding a few operational notes from the solutions side:
- Please include a small canonical prompt set (~30 prompts) that map to categories: short, medium, long, streaming-chunked.
- For each prompt include expected token counts and whether the client consumes tokens as they arrive (streaming) or waits for completion.
- Version control: prefix files with ACME_v1 and include a changelog entry when you update seed/traffic.

Repro steps we'll follow on our side:
- Run warmup (10m) -> 3 steady-state passes at target concurrency -> collect p50/p95, token histograms, and kernel traces.
- We'll publish a zip with raw logs, token timing CSVs, and an HTML perf dashboard.

Ben — quick ask: if we see >10% variance between runs, let's agree to run a controlled isolated pass (no other tenant noise) and record that as the canonical result.

Jordan — thanks for the fast turnaround on the seeds. If you can include a short doc note about any PII-sensitive prompts that must be redacted, that helps.

-Marissa
